A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Grounding-IQA work, with readable and directly matchable text, equations, figures, algorithms, and tables. Both end with references; neither includes the separately mentioned supplementary material, so this comparison covers all supplied content.

before.justification: v3 reports original fine-tuning experiments, ablations, and GIQA-Bench evaluations in Sections 4.2–4.3, Tables 2–5, and Figure 7.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results, including the ablations and quantitative and qualitative GIQA-Bench evaluations in Sections 4.2–4.3.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, IQA-Filter and Box-Merge procedures in Algorithm 1, coordinate representation, QA generation, and supervised fine-tuning method are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain GIQA-160K constructed from Q-Pathway and DQ-495K, covering natural, AI-generated, and artificially degraded images. GIQA-DES and GIQA-VQA evaluation on GIQA-Bench is unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2–5 retain the same corresponding comparators, including LLaVA and mPLUG-Owl2 variants, Shikra, Kosmos-2, Ferret, GroundingGPT, DepictQA-Wild, and Q-Instruct. The newly cited Jiang et al. work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Sections 3.4 and 4.1 retain the same benchmark composition, evaluation metrics, model configurations, and training settings. These include 100 GIQA-DES and 150 GIQA-VQA samples, two training epochs, and batch size 64.

E4.justification: The box-refinement and coordinate-representation ablations, multi-task training study, and model compatibility analysis in Tables 2–4 are unchanged. Figure 6's box-area distributions and Figure 7's qualitative comparisons are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All reported table values and graphical results are unchanged. For example, Table 5 retains Grounding-IQA(mPLUG-Owl2-7B)'s GIQA-DES LLM-Score of 63.00 and GIQA-VQA overall accuracy of 0.7417, with the same settings and comparisons.

T1.justification: The task definitions, coordinate mappings in Equations (1)–(2), and Tag-Recall definition are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: introducing grounding-IQA, constructing GIQA-160K through automated annotation, and establishing GIQA-Bench for fine-grained quality assessment.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of box refinement, coordinate discretization, multi-task training, and model performance. The explanation that VQA-only training limits grounding through reduced contextual information is unchanged, and no new limitations are introduced.

D1.justification: The annotation thresholds, coordinate grid, optimizer and training hyperparameters, four A100-80G GPUs, and code-access URL remain unchanged. The added funding acknowledgments provide no new implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 replaces one Ye et al. (2024) citation with Jiang et al. (2024), 'Effectiveness assessment of recent large vision-language models,' and adds that work to the references. Ye et al. remains cited elsewhere; the surrounding discussion and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 replaces the Preprint header with Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026, updates author affiliations, and adds an acknowledgments section before the references. The scientific narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment block shifts the reference list, and reference spacing and page breaks change. Figures 1–7, Tables 1–5, Algorithm 1, and their captions and placements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 updates publication and affiliation information, adds funding acknowledgments, and makes a limited citation addition. These changes improve attribution completeness but leave the scientific explanation, methods, experimental evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information unchanged, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
